english.title: Registered person fail to establish and operate systems to prevent abuse of service user resulting in harm or loss
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the

(A)_[service provider]_
(B)_[registered manager]_

in respect of a regulated activity, namely **(..SPECIFY ACTIVITY..), where systems and processes were not established and operated effectively to prevent abuse of service users in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..) resulting in

(C)_[avoidable harm to a service user, namely **(..SPECIFY SERVICE USER..)]_
(D)_[a service user, namely **(..SPECIFY SERVICE USER..), being exposed to a significant risk of avoidable harm occurring]_
(E)_[loss by a service user, namely **(..SPECIFY SERVICE USER..), of money or property resulting from theft, misuse or misappropriation of that money or property]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 13(2), 22(2) and 23(4) of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
were the registered person in respect of a registered activity
where systems and processes were not established and operated effectively to prevent abuse of service users
resulting in avoidable harm to a service user or
a service user being exposed to a significant risk of avoidable harm occurring or
loss by a service user of money or property resulting from theft, misuse or misappropriation of that money or property

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 8(1) and (2) provides that a registered person must comply with regulations 9 to 20A in carrying on a regulated activity, unless the thing to be done has by another registered person in relation to the regulated activity concerned.
(ii) As per regulation 22(4), it is a defence for a registered person to prove that they took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to prevent the breach.
